content:
Review request for two small Finset infrastructure PRs:

  • https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/pull/36003
  • https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/pull/36005

Both compile locally and CI is running.
Would love feedback on naming/placement/style.

I posted this on one of the PRs, but looking at the other the same applies to both. Both of these lemmas are just transitivity chains of existing lemmas, in obvious ways, so mathlib is probably better off without them.
Also, can you clarify the usage of AI in these PRs and their description?

Thanks Bhavik, super helpful feedback.

I agree both 36003 and 36005 are straightforward composition/transitivity chains of existing lemmas, so I’m going to close both and avoid adding this API surface.

On AI usage: I use AI tools for idea generation/drafting, but I choose the statements, edit/write the final Lean code, run local/CI checks, and take responsibility for what I submit.

I’ll focus next PRs on less-obvious, independently reusable contributions from my ever-evolving local lean library.
Thanks for the clarification and speedy response.
Most of #36063 seems to be copied from #33355 with your name put in the copyright/authors field. Is that intentional?

Hi @Bhavik Mehta and @Vlad Tsyrklevich and others, I want to offer a sincere apology for the overlap noise from my side, especially around #36063 while #33355 was already active. I should have coordinated first, that is on me.

I closed #36063, and I commented on #33355 to offer co-ownership and follow-up help in the original author’s preferred shape. Going forward, I will coordinate first whenever there is related active work, and avoid opening competing drafts.

I am very eager to contribute in good faith and be useful to this community. I come in peace, with respect for your time, and I am rigorously tracking these mistakes so they do not repeat. Thank you for the candid feedback, each comment is helping me become a better contributor.

Update
@Vlad Tsyrklevich I would never intentionally claim someone's work as my own. That you can count on. I also hope that as a Mathlib community we can assume good faith first.
